text:
maria: heads up — we had a small customer see 600 req/s bursts for ~8s and it tripped their quota enforcement. They got 429s for the tail of the burst. wondering if we should introduce a short holdback window + soft-penalty before hard throttles. :thinking:

jay: curious — is this per-key token bucket or org-level?

maria: per-key in this case. org has higher steady commit but key hit a rapid-fire client.

jon: quick notes: token-bucket gives natural bursts but if refill interval is coarse you can get microspikes causing queue pressure. leaky-bucket would smooth but adds latency/backpressure.

devon: agree. proposal: keep token-bucket for steady UX, but add a short "holdback" grace period (N seconds) where we respond with 202 + warning header or a low-priority queue instead of immediate 429. That buys time for KV cache warming and transient spikes.

alex: how would holdback interact with Dedicated vs Hosted? We can't delay requests for enterprise SLAs. Maybe make it configurable per plan.

maria: yes per-plan toggle. free tier -> short holdback + eventual hard 429. enterprise -> no holdback, or configurable policy via console.

jon: metrics to monitor: burst_length_seconds, burst_rate, dropped_after_holdback, avg_queue_time. need new telemetry buckets in console.

maria: +1. also want a dashboard card showing % requests that hit holdback vs direct 429s. important for support.

jay: operationally we could implement as two-tier enforcement: fast token-bucket check in the edge; if exceeded, call central enforcer with "allow_holdback=true" for Xs. central returns HOLD (enqueue metadata) or DENY. edge then either queue for short retry or return immediate 429.

devon: pseudocode: 
```
if (tokens > 0) { serve(); } else if (policy.holdback && burst_duration < policy.max_hold_s) { mark_holdback(); queue_short(); } else { deny(429); }
```

jon: important: keep the queued requests off the GPU frontends. we should use a small in-memory short-ttl queue in the edge router with backpressure to upstream. otherwise we risk head-of-line blocking.

maria: UX question for console: Should we expose holdback as an on/off toggle + two numbers (max_hold_s, max_queued)? or a templated policy like 'lenient|balanced|strict'?

alex: templated is easier for customers, toggle + advanced settings in enterprise. For observability show both policy and current counts.

jay: one risk: clients might exploit holdback by sending slow drip retries that keep consuming queued slots. need adaptive penalty: if same key hits holdback repeatedly over short window, apply exponential backoff and higher rejection rate.

devon: propose a short-term penalty token that reduces refill rate for key by factor f for M seconds after N holdbacks: effectively lowering burst budget. easier than blacklisting.

maria: example config suggestion: 
```
policy: {
  type: "token_bucket",
  capacity: 200,
  refill_per_sec: 20,
  holdback: { enabled: true, max_hold_s: 10, max_queue: 30 },
  penalty: { enabled: true, factor: 0.5, window_s: 60, threshold: 3 }
}
```

jon: we should test with a synthetic 10s aggressive spike + normal background to measure SLA impact. add canary with 5% traffic first.

infra-bot: canary deploy queued: quota-holdback-v1 to edge cluster a at 2026-04-02T17:02:10Z

sre-bot: alert rule suggestion: if holdback_rate > 5% for 5m AND dropped_after_holdback > 1% => page oncall.

maria: thanks — I'll draft RFC with the config schema, telemetry keys, and default templates. plan to run load tests and a 5% canary next week.

jay: one more thought — documentation should show recommended client retry strategy: jittered exponential backoff + respect Retry-After header for holdback.

alex: :thumbsup: if RFC includes console widgets and an exportable CSV for support cases then i'm sold.

maria: will include. pulling together RFC now.

devon: if you want i can prototype in the edge router this afternoon.

maria: that'd be awesome — ping me when done. :shipit:
